questions.text:
Let # be a binary operator defined as
X#Y=X'+Y' where X and Y are Boolean variables.
Consider the following two statements.

(S1) (P # Q) # R = P # (Q # R)
(S2) Q # R = R # Q

Which of the following is/are true for the Boolean variables P, Q and R?
questions.solution:
X # Y = X' + Y' = (XY)', i.e. NAND.

- S2: NAND is commutative [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- S1: (P # Q) # R = PQ + R', while P # (Q # R) = P' + QR. Different (e.g. P = 0, R = 1) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: Only S2 is true

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Both S1 and S2 are true
Neither S1 nor S2 are true

questions.text:
Consider a software project with the following information domain characteristics for calculation of function point metric.
Number of external inputs (I) = 30
Number of external outputs (O) = 60
Number of external inquiries (E) = 23
Number of files (F) = 08
Number of external interfaces (N) = 02

It is given that the complexity weighting factors for I, O, E, F and N are 4, 5, 4, 10 and 7, respectively. It is also given that, out of fourteen value adjustment factors that influence the development effort, four factors are not applicable, each of the other four factors have value 3, and each of the remaining factors have value 4. The computed value of function point metric is _____________.
questions.solution:
UFP = 30 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 + 60 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 + 23 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 + 8 [latex]\times[/latex] 10 + 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 7 = 120 + 300 + 92 + 80 + 14 = 606

Sum of factors = 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 0 + 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 + 6 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 = 36

FP = 606 [latex]\times[/latex] (0.65 + 0.01 [latex]\times[/latex] 36) = 606 [latex]\times[/latex] 1.01 = 612.06

Answer: 612.06

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: In a web server, ten WebPages are stored with the URLs of the form http://www.yourname.com/var.html; where, var is a different number from 1 to 10 for each Webpage. Suppose, the client stores the Webpage with var =1 (say W1) in local machine, edits and then tests. Rest of the WebPages remains on the web server. W1 contains several relative URLs of the form "var.html" referring to the other WebPages. Which one of the following statements needs to be added in W1, so that all the relative URLs in W1 refer to the appropriate WebPages on the web server?
questions.solution:
The HTML base tag sets the base URL for all relative links in the page. With base href = "http://www.yourname.com/", the link "var.html" points to the page on the server.

Answer: base href: "http://www.yourname.com/"

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
I. TCP connections are full duplex
II. TCP has no option for selective acknowledgement
III. TCP connections are message streams
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: TCP connections are full duplex [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II: TCP has a SACK (selective acknowledgement) option [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- III: TCP is a byte stream, not a message stream [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: Only I is correct

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Only I and III are correct
Only II and III are correct
All of I, II and III are correct

questions.text:
Consider the equality [latex]\sum_{i=0}^{n}i^{3}=X[/latex] and the following choices for X
I.[latex] \Theta (n^{4}) [/latex]
II. [latex] \Theta (n^{5}) [/latex]
III. [latex]O (n^{5}) [/latex]
IV. [latex] \Omega (n^{3})[/latex]
The equality above remains correct if X is replaced by
questions.solution:
[latex]\sum_{i=0}^n i^3=\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)^2=\Theta(n^4)[/latex]

A [latex]\Theta(n^4)[/latex] function is also [latex]O(n^5)[/latex] and [latex]\Omega(n^3)[/latex], but it is not [latex]\Theta(n^5)[/latex].

Answer: I or III or IV but not II

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: I or III or IV but not II
II or III or IV but not I
